title: HeimdallJob@1
description: The universal unit of work (spec §3). Holodeck stops asking for a particular model and submits one of these instead; Heimdall resolves it to an executor. A model field is a pin, and pins exist only when a user explicitly names one.

taskClass.description: Dotted class from src/job.js TASK_CLASSES; routing evidence is keyed on this.

objective.description: interactive optimizes time-to-acceptable-answer; batch may trade time for money/energy.

routing.description: The objective the router minimizes (src/escalation.js choose). fastest = E[time-to-accepted]; cheapest = E[cost-per-accepted], gated by the job's own local acceptance checks. null derives from objective (batch -> cheapest). A cheapest pick is only ever kept when acceptance passes; a failing proposal escalates, never downgrades.

parts.description: A COMPOSITE job: sub-tasks pulled apart by capability, each routed on its own (src/compose.js) and merged by the SYSTEM, never a model. A part needing native-tools (taskClass mechanical.tool) can only reach a model that advertises tools, so tool-calling splits from generation. null = inferred mechanically from `requires`/`protocols`, or a single whole.

merge.description: How a composite job's part proposals are merged — by the system: byPart = { byPart: {id: proposal}, text }; text adds the concatenation; fields additionally flattens object parts. Default byPart.

privacy.description: local-raw = executor inside the trust domain sees raw spans; sealed-external = the provider receives only the external projection (spec §2.I).

effects.description: Derived mechanically from the required Doors where possible (spec §3).

requires.description: Door names the job needs, e.g. door:find, door:read.

inputs.description: Handles (F12, R18) the job is about.

protocols.description: Action modes the executor may use; native-tools is an optimization, never a requirement (spec §5).

model.description: Explicit pin only — set when a user pins a model, never by default.

task.description: Plain statement of what needs solving (escalation design 2026-10; docs/ESCALATION.md).

disclosure.description: What may leave this machine for the job, least to most permissive. Defaults from `privacy` (local-raw -> none, sealed-external -> sealed-external-text). A route's exposure may never exceed it, and escalation never raises it.

acceptance.description: Typed checks the Fold runs LOCALLY on a returned proposal; the proposal becomes `accepted` only when all pass (src/acceptance.js).

falsifyingControl: a job whose effects do not cover every required Door's effect, or a sealed-external job whose requires contains an operation that cannot be projected, contradicts the contract
